description: Mitigations for vehicle-pedestrian strikes. Segregation is the dominant control — keep people and vehicles apart.

mitigations.name: segregation_design
mitigations.description: Physical separation of pedestrian and vehicle routes by design. Raised walkways, separate access routes, physical barriers (jersey barriers, bollards). Inherent to site layout.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.02. Design feature — can't be bypassed easily. Failure: gaps in barrier coverage, shared zones at loading/delivery points.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: If pedestrians and vehicles are physically separated, strikes cannot occur. Effectiveness limited by transition zones where separation breaks down.

mitigations.name: speed_controls
mitigations.description: Speed humps, speed limiters on vehicles, radar speed signs. Reduces kinetic energy at impact. Tefft 2013: 10mph reduction halves pedestrian fatality risk.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05 for physical speed controls (humps). Higher PFD for electronic limiters that can be overridden.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Tefft 2013 dose-response: reducing speed from 30mph to 20mph reduces pedestrian fatality from ~40% to ~10%. Speed controls don't prevent the strike but dramatically reduce severity.

mitigations.name: reversing_aids
mitigations.description: Reversing cameras, proximity sensors, radar on vehicles. Alerts driver to pedestrians in blind spot. Most effective for low-speed reversing strikes.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.08. Failure: camera obscured, driver doesn't check display, sensor false alarms leading to alarm fatigue.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: NHTSA: rear cameras reduce backing crashes by ~17% overall, much higher for pedestrian-behind-vehicle scenarios.

mitigations.name: high_vis
mitigations.description: EN ISO 20471 high-visibility clothing. Makes pedestrians visible to drivers. PPE — human-dependent (must be worn, must be clean, limited effectiveness in poor visibility).
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.10 for PPE. Failure: not worn, dirty/faded, insufficient lighting for fluorescent material, driver looking elsewhere.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Improves driver detection of pedestrians. Limited effectiveness — being visible doesn't prevent a strike if the driver isn't looking or can't stop in time.

mitigations.name: banksman_spotter
mitigations.description: Trained spotter guiding vehicle movements in shared zones. Human control — guides the driver and warns pedestrians.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Failure: banksman distracted, not positioned correctly, communication breakdown, driver proceeds without banksman for 'quick' move.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Effective when banksman is competent and driver follows instructions. Human-dependent — both parties must perform.

sources.author: Tefft
sources.relevance: Impact speed and pedestrian risk — dose-response for speed controls
